document: Fund Covid booster vaccines for all, with priority for Long Covid sufferers, Long Covid can ruin lives and cause financial hardship so we believe the Government must try to prevent new Covid infections. We want free Covid booster vaccines for all and Long Covid sufferers should be a prioritised group., Currently, many Long Covid sufferers are unable to protect themselves against Covid, which is circulating widely. Research shows repeat infections can cause increasingly severe Long Covid symptoms so we believe sufferers should be considered as medically vulnerable. We think the best way to help prevent repeat infections for existing sufferers is by prioritising vaccination for those who have Long Covid. A full vaccine roll-out could also help prevent new cases of Long Covid by reducing the total number of Covid cases in circulation. Long Covid affects thousands and a recent study estimated that it could cost the economy up to £20 billion due to lost working days.

Introduce new air quality and PPE rules for health and social care settings, We want the Government to set new rules on air quality and infection control in health and social care settings, to prevent and control airborne infections, with new ventilation and filtration requirements, new PPE standards and staffing rules, and monitoring and inspection to ensure compliance., Covid and other infectious diseases are spread by airborne aerosols. There are key ways to prevent them, by improving air quality and using well-fitting respiratory masks. Some research has found that reinfection can increase the risk of long-term serious organ damage and care workers having amongst the highest prevalence of long Covid. There are many tools to protect people in health and social care, including improving ventilation/air filtration, reintroducing PPE masks and Covid testing, and supporting ill staff to stay home.

Legally recognise Non-Binary as a gender, Many non-binary people in the UK currently feel invisible and ignored. Therefore, we think this government should seek to reform the Gender Recognition Act 2004 so that it extends legal recognition to a third, non-binary gender., Currently non-binary people are not recognised in UK law. This means that we have no choice but to choose either male or female gender markers on government IDs and in many other institutional settings. This can lead to constant misgendering. Therefore, we think the government should legally recognise non-binary people to allow us to be seen as our true gender by society and to help us feel more respected in everyday life. We think that this would be in line with fundamental British values.

Conduct a review of routes into work for new graduates., We believe that many graduates, myself included, who spent £27k+ on university are struggling to find jobs. Entry-level roles often demand experience, which feels unfair, as we're constantly rejected for lacking it. We need opportunities, yet many of us lack industry connections., We want the Government to review the job opportunities available to new graduates and how graduates can get the experience necessary to do those jobs.  
Please help to give us a chance.

Require more qualifications for teachers/teaching assistants at SEN schools, We want the government to create a policy to require more training courses for individuals working within special educational schools. We think teachers should be required to do an extra year on top of their PGCE to get a specialised SEN teaching qualification., We also think all teaching assistants should be level 2 SEN qualified.

We think these schools need professionals who are trained so they can support each child with their different needs. That could be communicating in different ways or coping with day-to-day struggles.

We believe that teachers need specific qualifications and should only be teaching with a specific SEN teacher qualification. This is paramount.

Create a national badge for parent and child spaces., I would like a badge introduced for parent and child spaces so others don't park there. We think the government should create a yellow badge for parents of children up to the age of 12 which enables them to park in parent and child spaces. , I am a new father to a child and many a time from When my child has come out of hospital me and my partner have had difficulty because we've had to park in a smaller normal space and struggle to get the pram and baby out or when it's raining we've had to park far away because someone with no children or a blue badge has parked in some of the spaces meant for parents and children.

National measures to prevent people leaving dog faeces on the streets., We are calling for the Government to require schools to educate children, from infant school age, on the dangers of owners not picking up their dog's faeces. We also want the Government to increase default fines and give more funding for local authority enforcement.,  
Our communities are littered with dog faeces left on streets and in parks by irresponsible dog owners. We feel this is ruining the enjoyment of green areas and causing a public health concern.
It might be taken into classrooms and homes on shoes, prams and wheelchairs. If children and babies play amongst traces of faeces it can cause serious health concerns.

Enact the Socio-Economic Duty of the Equality Act 2010., To enact the Socio-Economic Duty of the Equality Act 2010.
This requires public bodies to consider inequalities resulting from socio-economic disadvantage when making certain decisions. Successive governments have not enacted the Duty., We think income and wealth inequalities have devastating effects on the lives of the working class in the UK. We think the Equality Act 2010 was a significant step in tackling social and economic inequalities. Chief amongst its measures was the Socio-economic Duty, ‘designed to reduce the inequalities of outcome which result from socio-economic disadvantage’.
We think the unenacted first part of the Equality Act can help initiate a wider change in tackling entrenched class discrimination.

Allow transgender people to self-identify their legal gender., We believe the government should change legislation to make it easier for trans people of all ages to change their legal gender without an official diagnosis of gender dysphoria., Transgender people have a history of major discrimination in the UK and around the world. Major studies in reputable journals have shown a positive correlation between allowing trans people to live as their gender, rather than their sex assigned at birth in regards to positive mental and physical health outcomes.

Provide schools with money to fund teaching assistants in every class., I am a teacher of over 10 years. I think the classroom environment has never been so difficult. 11 years ago I had a full time TA and teacher workload seemed ‘less’. I think teachers, fantastic long term teachers, are leaving the profession due to lack of support., Give schools money specifically for teaching assistants. We think each class should have a TA, where possible. We are trying to create scientists, mathematicians, shop workers etc yet without support we can’t inspire. We believe we are fighting fires to attend needs and behaviour over teaching. We think teaching assistants are the glue, they’re what teachers need to function, support, challenge, inspire and teach the interventions the teachers need to support the children in need.

Don't apply VAT to independent school fees, or remove business rates relief., Prevent independent schools from having to pay VAT on fees and incurring business rates as a result of new legislation., We think the Government needs to understand that not all independent school parents are wealthy, appreciate the benefits of independent schools and do better due diligence.
Independent schools have supported Ukrainian refugees, children with SEN, sharing facilities with public schools and supporting less fortunate families with bursaries. 
We think this policy will split children from established friend networks, familiar environments and place the burden and cost on public schools.

Provide funding to optical services to pay for BSL interpreters, Provide Government funding to optical services, so that they can pay to book BSL interpreters for deaf patients. I am a dispensing optician who has seen many deaf patients in recent years., The cost of a BSL interpreter for a single visit by far outweighs the current private or NHS sight test fees (even if NHS optical vouchers were included). This means that not all opticians can afford to provide support to their deaf patients, leading to potential communication barriers and unequal access to eyecare.

Free use of parking areas and drop-off and pick-up zones at airports for taxi's, Free use of parking areas and drop-off and pick-up zones at airports for any taxi drivers from any county., All taxis have the right to use airport areas without paying. Just like buses and trains. We also provide the same service. Airport transfers. And pick-ups. Keep an eye on illegal transporters. Taxi drivers try to survive with competition from unlicensed people who are dedicated to taking people to airports.

Make hedgehog highways mandatory on all new fencing., Hedgehogs travel around one mile every night through our parks and gardens in their quest to find enough food and a mate. We can make their life a little easier by removing the barriers within our control. For example, by mandating the use of holes/hedgehog friendly gravel boards on all new fencing., Surveys in the latest ‘State of Britain's Hedgehogs’ report estimate that hedgehog numbers have decreased by up to 75% in rural areas since the turn of the century. Much of this decline can be attributed to human expansion and the erection of fencing which hedgehogs (and other treasured wildlife) cannot gain access through.

Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal, We want all forms of geo-engineering to be illegal in the UK. We do not want any use of technologies to intervene in the Earth's natural systems., We think there is a potential for this to negatively impact humanity, flora and fauna in the future. It has previously been said that Greenhouse Gas Removal (GGR) is essential to meet climate targets. We believe that this, and all other forms of geo-engineering, should be made illegal in the UK.

Scrap the APD increase for essential regional flights and consider a reform, Reverse the increases made in the Budget to Air Passenger Duty (APD) on regional air routes which are essential to connectivity in the UK, whilst also considering a reform which will safeguard these routes for future generations with lower APD offered on a case-by-case basis., APD disproportionately affects regional flights as it is levied on both legs of a return journey. This means that regional airline operations become financially unsustainable.
 
Regional flights can massively benefit small communities where other modes of transport are not viable for day returns either for business or visiting friends and relatives.
 
APD is not and never has been an environmental tax. We believe that the UK regional sector is already at the forefront of decarbonisation efforts.

Make autism training mandatory for teachers in schools to help understanding, We would like the Government to make autism training mandatory for all teachers., I believe that if teachers were made to complete autism training as a mandatory requirement, this would give them some understanding of how people living with Autism can struggle in school and how best they can support their students as currently there is very little understanding with in schools. I think that this may also help some children remain in mainstream schools instead of having to go to specialist schools, as the child may not actually need to attend a specialist school if mainstream ones could support.

Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal., We believe neither the Government, nor anyone else, should be able to use technologies to intervene in the Earth’s natural weather systems. WE WANT ALL FORMS of 'GEO-ENGINEERING' on LAND, SEA & AIR in the UK BANNED., The Govt has 'declared Geo-Engineering essential to meet its climate targets'. We strongly counter this claim. People, animals, plants are being harmed; because the atmosphere in which they exist is being polluted on a daily basis by a cocktail of dangerous, chemicals and heavy metals they should NOT be exposed to. More importantly WE WERE NOT ASKED for our opinion nor permission to put our health at risk for the sake of a 'globalist' Net Zero agenda. NOR SHOULD OUR GOVERNMENT IMPOSE IT!

Allow other religions to solemnise weddings , Change the law so that any faith leader registered as such, has the right to conduct weddings equal to Anglican, Quaker and Jewish leaders., We think the current rules regarding weddings are outdated and favour Anglican, Quaker and Jewish leaders over other religions or faiths, giving greater religious power to clergy from 3 faith groups over any other. We think that legal bias needs to end.

We believe a lot of the population feel let down by the rules some Churches have that say they cannot have a religious wedding. Other faith leaders may be willing to conduct the wedding for same-sex or mixed faith couples.

Create a single, UK-wide exemption certificate for XL Bullies, I believe responsible owners of XL bullies are being unfairly restricted in many ways, despite the coordinated approach being taken by all nations in relation to exemption rules. I propose the Government create a single, UK-wide certificate for exempted XL bullies., This would be to allow responsible dog owners to travel freely within the UK as long as the rules are followed. I believe that due to these rules, people who follow these rules cannot visit friends or family who live in Scotland from England or vice versa or cannot go on holiday in other UK nations. I also believe it is now difficult to find suitable boarding or sitters as many may not take XL Bullies.

Fund a new COPD strategy, including psychological interventions, We urge Parliament to help improve Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) outcomes by funding the development of a new COPD Strategy., We would like the strategy to include:
- psychological screening and mental health intervention.
- funded COPD research to explore potential holistic care.
- raising awareness to help reduce stigma.
It is estimated COPD affects over a million people in the UK, costing the NHS an estimated £1.9 billion annually. Despite this, we believe that it is underfunded, stigmatized, and poorly integrated into care.

Reduce VAT for hospitality businesses, I believe that businesses in the hospitality sector could be helped by reducing VAT to a lower rate. I think it would allow the survival of more hospitality businesses and others that might be struggling due to current rates of VAT.,

Improve mental health services for neurodiverse young people, We call on the Government to increase funding for NHS Child and Adolescents Mental Health Services to enable early diagnosis, intervention, treatment and support for children who are neurodiverse. We believe CAMHS requires more funding to improve staffing, treatment and care problems., We believe NHS children and adolescent mental health services are failing our children with neurodiversity, and that early intervention, diagnosis, treatment and support are integral to enabling them to thrive. We believe that the Government is underfunding these services, putting the health and wellbeing of our young people at tremendous risk.

Tax banks to recoup the £23bn they lost taxpayers in the banking crisis, To recoup the outstanding/lost £23bn from the financial/banking sector, following the bailout during the financial crisis. We think this should be recouped through emergency taxation on banks, and that this could be used to fill what has been described as £22bn black hole in public finances., The Government have said there is a £22bn black hole in the public finances. We are told by the Chancellor the country is in trouble. We think it will be every day people, pensioners, small businesses and farmers who are going to pick up the tab. The Government bailed out the banks and other institutions in the City of London in 2008. We think it is time for them to return the favour, return the money they took and return the budget back to black.

Review the issuing of hormone prescriptions for transgender individuals by GPs, I believe the government should launch a review into the ways that GPs work alongside NHS gender clinics to issue prescriptions for hormones., It has been reported that some transgender individuals have been refused prescriptions for hormone medication, or had them withdrawn, despite having a gender dysphoria diagnosis. Hormones are extremely important to many transgender people and can help them cope with symptoms of gender dysphoria. Not having access to hormones may also affect access to further treatment.

Free hospital parking for all NHS staff in England , We think NHS staff should not have to pay to park on-site at hospitals. Staff don’t have to pay to park in Wales or Scotland. We want free parking for NHS staff please!, Because we think nobody should be turning up to work in a hospital who has spent time searching for a parking space and then paying an exorbitantly high charge for it. Especially when they may find, if they worked elsewhere it would be different. We think standard free parking for all staff is what is needed.

Assisted Dying Should Not be Legalised in the UK. Please sign before 29 Nov., We, the undersigned, are pleading that this Government reject the Leadbeater Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.
This Bill is a tragedy.
It’s a Slippery Slope into untold sadness. 
We say, “NO.”, This Bill is a Pandora’s Box of unstoppable tragedies - a legal and moral nightmare. Horrifying stories from countries where assisted dying is legal, warn us that safeguards are easily eroded. As boundaries disappear and financial pressures rise, the most vulnerable are at risk - the elderly, disabled, poor, depressed. They should be loved, valued and protected, not left feeling that it’s better to die than to be a burden on others. And it could be you or me. 
Where is love? 
“Care, not Killing”

Review regulation of gambling self-exclusion schemes, I call on the Government to review the regulation of gambling self-exclusion schemes, as I believe it is too easy for people to bypass self-exclusion systems. , Gambling companies are required by their licences to check self-exclusions lists. But being a recovering addict, I always found a way to join sites by a change in name, spelling, mixing around words in my address, different emails etc from the ones I registered with the self-exclusion site. The worst of my gambling was 2023 and I self-excluded in 2020 for 5 years. I think this should never have been allowed to happen and the rules should be changed to strengthen ID verification.

NO VAT ON PRIVATE SCHOOLS, Cancel VAT on private schools , many parents working on the breadline just to give their children a better chance of education ., Adding VAT to private schools has effected many parents heavily to the degree they have had to pull out their children from a better chance of education , and send them to government schools , adding more pressure to the government schools as well as ruining a better opportunity of education for their children overall .

Update the Health and Safety at Work Act to be gender neutral, I believe this law uses outdated gendered language like “his employees”, and that it should be updated to be more inclusive as it applies to everyone regardless of their gender. I believe updating this language would reflect the UK’s commitment to fairness, equality, and respect for all workers. , By replacing words like “his” with “their,” I think the Government can encourage a sense of respect and belonging for all. As the Employment Rights Bill will aim to strengthen measures on sexual harassment prevention, many are shocked to see how exclusionary this language remains in the Health and Safety at Work Act. I believe updating the Act would be a meaningful step towards greater inclusivity.

Fully Repeal the Gender Recognition Act, The Government should repeal the Gender Recognition Act (GRA) 2004., We believe that the GRA 2004 was created on a basis of fore-grounding the personal autonomy, personal development and security of a very small minority of UK citizens. In so doing, we think it had the effect of diminishing and displacing the Human Rights, safety, autonomy and dignity of over 50% of the UK population - namely women. We therefore think that it needs now to be repealed

Review how to close the gender health gap and improve women's healthcare, I want the government to hold a review into how to close the gender health gap, and prioritise women’s health and wellbeing more both in workplace & personal life. This should consider how women suffering from endometriosis & other conditions affecting women should be given help, support & education, We think there is a lack of support and urgency from doctors to help women with issues such as periods and endometriosis. Women can face long waiting lists. Waiting is not only hard for the symptoms but the weight on your mental health is alot! We think this review should consider whether there needs to be more funding and more help, so women can be seen quicker & to help understand why our bodies do what they do. Women deserve to be heard!

Regulate Generative AI imagery, We think Generative AI for commercial use like advertising must be banned and companies must disclose using AI and list the prompts used. We think it must be made illegal to access AI "nudify" apps and websites, and AI generated imagery must require a watermark disclosing that it is AI generated., We think over-reliance on AI has lead to rampant misinformation, false-advertising and scams becoming commonplace. We feel you can no longer perform a simple image search without being bombarded with AI generated results which do not disclose the fact they were made with AI.

AI deepfakes are being used to create pornographic imagery of non-consenting women. We think this must be made illegal and the use of all Generative AI whether for commercial or personal use must be disclosed.

Abolish VAT on fitness services, We believe the fitness industry plays a crucial role in promoting physical, mental, and emotional health across the UK. We call on the Government to abolish VAT on all fitness services, including gym memberships, classes, and personal training. , We think this would make exercise more accessible and affordable for everyone.

The pandemic has highlighted the importance of physical and mental health, yet the cost of accessing fitness services can be a barrier for many. We think abolishing VAT on fitness services would be an investment in the nation's health and a step towards a healthier, more resilient society.
 
By removing VAT, gyms and fitness providers could lower their prices, which may encourage more people to prioritise their health and well-being.

Remove the Asset Purchase Facility Deed of Indemnity , Since 2009, UK Taxpayers have been on the financial hook for losses by the Bank of England’s Quantitative Easing Policy. We think removing the deed of Indemnity against the UK Taxpayer would save the Treasury a significant sum annually., Remove the Deed of Indemnity!
 
The Bank of England and the Treasury came up with this indemnity policy that we think is idiosyncratic and is estimated to cost the U.K Taxpayer over the lifetime of the policy in excess of £100 Billion.
We think that by removing the Indemnity policy it would be a simple fix to help the UK's Fiscal problems.

By removing the Indemnity policy it will be a simple fix to the UKs Fiscal problems.

Remove actively farmed land from IHT valuations, We think when calculating IHT, land which which is actively farmed should be removed from the valuation of the estate., Thus, actively working farms will continue to benefit from their special status, and we think recent changes could be focussed on those seeking merely to avoid IHT.
Checks and balances, and other safeguards can be brought into play, such as farms continue to be actively farmed for x number of years post estate transfer.

Ban isolation in schools, I believe there is an urgent need to ban isolation in schools. I consider such practices harm vulnerable students, including autistic children, violating their rights and well-being and schools must adopt inclusive, supportive strategies to ensure a safe, nurturing environment for all children., I believe that punishments in schools disproportionately target children with Special Educational Needs (SEN), intensifying their struggles. Isolation and similar practices exacerbate anxiety, depression, and feelings of exclusion, severely impacting mental health. I believe there is a need to replace harmful disciplinary measures with tailored support systems that nurture inclusion and emotional growth. It’s imperative to protect SEN students' well-being and rights immediately.

Make all forms of geo-engineering affecting the environment illegal, We believe that neither the government, nor anyone else, should be able to use technologies to intervene in the Earth's natural systems. 
We want all forms of geo-engineering on land, sea and air to be banned., The government has said geo-engineering is essential to meet its climate targets:

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/geo-engineering-research-the-government-s-view/9d532e11-2980-4336-abdf-e1ef7f669949#why-they-are-needed

We want geo-engineering to be banned.

Compensate people excluded from Government COVID support schemes, 1. Acknowledge the financial hardship faced by taxpayers excluded from government support during COVID

2. Provide fair & equitable redress to those taxpayer who received nothing, We think an estimated 3 million UK taxpayers, comprising a diverse group of freelancers, small business owners, & newly employed individuals, were unfairly excluded from COVID financial support schemes. We believe this exclusion resulted in severe financial hardship, including loss of income, business closures, & personal debt. Despite repeated calls for action, we feel the government has failed in its moral obligation & legal duty to address this social injustice, which we think continues to wreck lives.

Fund improved care and support for individuals with FASD., Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is a disability affecting both children and adults, but there is a lack of awareness among healthcare professionals and the public. Consequently, individuals with FASD can struggle to access appropriate care and support services., We urge the Government to increase funding that goes towards improving care and support for individuals with FASD by:

1. Increasing funding for research into effective interventions and treatments
2. Funding the development of comprehensive training programs for healthcare professionals on how best to diagnose and treat individuals with FASD
3. Providing increased resources for families caring for loved ones with FASD
4. Funding public awareness activities about the risks associated with alcohol consumption during pregnancy

We believe it is time for the Government to take action on this critical issue affecting so many lives across our country. We urge it to act swiftly in implementing these changes so that individuals affected by FASD can receive the care they need.

Remove VAT on life saving equipment, I want the government to remove VAT on life saving equipment. I wanted to purchase a defibrillator for residents in my area to use and was stunned to learn it was not VAT exempt., I think this could save lives.

Make it mandatory that all employers have Autism Awareness training, 7 in 10 autistic people are unemployed This is largely due to a lack of awareness and reluctance from employers to make reasonable adjustments for autistic employees. To address this, I propose making it mandatory for all employers to undergo autism awareness training., The Autism Act 2009 aimed to improve support and create more opportunities for autistic people. However, despite the Act's provisions, progress has been limited since its publication. Authorities have cited allocated budgets for promoting equality and diversity for autistic individuals, but there is ongoing evidence that they continue to face significant challenges in various aspects of daily life.

Review care for sickle cell patients within the NHS, We consider that there is systemic poor care and racial disparities in NHS healthcare for sickle cell patients, and that there needs to be a review into this. , This should include looking into necessary training for professionals on sickle cell disease, establishing treatment centres with resources for pain management, and promoting diversity within the NHS to ensure equitable care for all.
 
Enough is Enough! We believe that the NHS have neglected sickle cell patients and it has gone on for far too long. We can no longer stand by while lives are lost. The lives of sickle cell patients matter. It’s time to take action.

Protect our freedoms: Ban facial recognition of public, We urge the government to ban the use of mass facial recognition technology in public spaces. We believe legislation is needed to protect rights and ensure ethical use of technology., We believe it threatens privacy, freedom, & democracy, enables intrusive surveillance, undermines public trust, & disproportionately impacts marginalised groups through bias & misidentification. We think it impacts lawful protests & sets a dangerous precedent for unchecked monitoring. We think without legislation, the UK risks becoming a surveillance state, eroding civil liberties & democratic values. We believe a ban is essential to protect freedoms, ensure accountability & uphold human rights.

Petition Against Closure of Adult Education Centres & Creative Courses In Kent, numerous courses being closed from July 2025 with centres being shut down completely.
These courses and centres provide important classes for all including creaticlve classes, wellbeing,  occupational therapy and rehabilitation as well as equipping people with the skills to return to the workplace., Please can you get this petition considered as the centres and classes are important to so many Please can you get this petition considered as the centres and classes are important to see theo many from a mental health and personal development point of view

Increase funding for medical research on women's anatomy, Prioritise and allocate more funding for medical research on women's anatomy. We believe this will help to ensure a future where women’s health is understood, valued, and advanced for generations to come., Historically, medical research has disproportionately focused on men’s bodies. We believe this has left gaps in the understanding and treatment of conditions unique to or more prevalent in women. We think this lack of investment in women’s health could have contributed to delayed diagnoses, inadequate treatments, and preventable suffering for millions of women across the UK. 
 
By funding dedicated research on women’s bodies, the Government could help address these inequalities, improve health outcomes, and pave the way for a healthcare system that truly supports everyone. We believe it’s time to close the gender health gap and ensure that women’s health is not an afterthought.

Allow tax relief on training for self-employed people to set up new businesses, We would like the government to allow full tax relief for training costs for people starting a new business or expanding into new areas of business that are not directly related to what they currently do., I recently set up a new business and incurred significant training costs. I was shocked to discover that there is no tax relief for training to enable new business setup or for business expansion.
 
We feel that training costs, especially for businesses requiring qualifications, can be a significant barrier to entry for potential entrepreneurs and that self-employed people and small businesses already have a disproportionate tax burden.
 
We believe that successful economies support growth of new and small businesses.

School Minibus Safety - Remove Section 19 Exemptions for Schools, We call on the Government to remove Section 19 exemptions for schools in the Transport Act 1985, so children and young people are only driven by qualified, professional drivers, and that minibuses are maintained to commercial standards, by requiring a full Public Service Vehicle Operator’s Licence., In November 1993, a minibus carrying young people home to a Worcestershire school from a school trip to London crashed into a lorry, killing 13 people. The trip took place after the school day and the crash occurred just after midnight. We lost our daughter Claire in that crash.
A teacher, or support staff member can still, thirty years later, work all day, and then drive a school minibus for long distances without further training or qualifications.
All children, young people and staff must Come Home Safe.

Review law around consent and disclosing sex or trans identity, We believe the law needs reviewing regarding consent in rape cases & disclosing birth sex. We are concerned that there could be insufficient protections against criminalisation for trans &  non-binary people who are questioning their gender & are not ready to have a conversation about their gender. ,

Change dangerous junction of Croxteth Hall Lane with Oak Lane, We have dangerous junction of Croxteth Hall Lane with Oak Lane the left hand turn Lane onto Croxteth Park Estate is abused by drivers going straight on instead. We have many examples by residents feeling scared attempting a right turn onto the estate., The junction is an accident black spot and many drivers jump the red lights causing a danger to those turning right onto Croxteth Park Estate.
We need a review of the options to improve the safety of this junction to widen the left hand turn only lane or create 3 distinct lanes one for turning right into oak Lane one for straight ahead and one for turn left only. The road markings and signage are not clear enough for drivers not familiar to the area and this is unsafe for all road users.

Reopen City and Sandwell Hospitals within the SWBH NHS Trust, We call on the Government to reopen City and Sandwell Hospitals, which were closed to make way for the MMUH Hospital. The new hospital does not match the combined capacity of the two former hospitals, leaving local communities with reduced access to vital healthcare services., City and Sandwell Hospitals were closed to consolidate services at the new MMUH Hospital. However, the new hospital lacks the capacity to fully replace both facilities, resulting in longer wait times, reduced access to care, and overcrowding. Patients, especially vulnerable groups, now face increased difficulties in obtaining timely treatment. Reopening these hospitals would restore essential services, relieve pressure on the NHS, and address the growing demand for healthcare in the region.

Ban Applied Behaviour Analysis Therapy designed to reduce Autistic Stimming, The Government should ban Applied Behaviour Analysis Therapy (“ABA”), for the purpose of reducing soothing “stimming” behaviours in people with autism spectrum disorder., Reports indicate that people with autism spectrum disorder call ABA therapy “abusive” or “traumatic” and some may have c-PTSD as a result.
 
Furthermore, research from the US Department of Defence concluded that ABA is not significantly improving outcomes.

Mandate that all dentists provide minimum amount of NHS services, Millions lack NHS dental care. We demand a 50% NHS allocation mandate for all dentist practices, requirements to ensure all NHS treatment that is needed for a particular patient is carried out, and a rule requiring practices to accept new NHS patients in their area., We don't think dental care should be dependent on income. An estimated 13 million lack NHS dental care, with many unable to access treatment at all. Those who do can face inadequate care and struggle to get all the treatments they may need. Some practices only treat private patients, leaving locals excluded. A 50% mandate, requirements to ensure full and NHS treatment is carried out, and ensuring local NHS access could reduce inequality, tackle the dental crisis, and protect public health.

I propose that we reinstate treason laws, I would like to see treasonous activity punishable by the most severe laws, like it used to be., It was a bad decision for treason laws to be removed. It has allowed many to act treasonously and not be held to account.

It’s one of the most serious crimes and should be enforced as so

Make Pathological Demand Avoidance a formal diagnosis & support for families, I am petitioning for Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA) to be formally recognized and diagnosed within the healthcare and educational systems. PDA is a complex profile of autism characterized by extreme anxiety which can significantly impact individuals and their families., Despite growing awareness and research, many individuals with PDA struggle to receive appropriate support due to a lack of formal diagnostic recognition. This results in misdiagnosis, inadequate interventions, and a lack of tailored resources. Formal recognition will lead to earlier diagnosis, better understanding, and improved outcomes for individuals and their families.

Allow more healthcare workers to display green beacons when on call, Amend the Road Vehicle Lighting Regulations 1989 to allow National Midwifery Council and Heath and Care Professions Council registered healthcare professionals and Community First Responders dispatched on behalf of state ambulance services to use green beacons in addition to GMC registered doctors., The Road Vehicle Lighting Regs 1989 permit the display of green beacons by GMC registered doctors.
 
Green beacons do not give exemptions to traffic rules but they can ease passage through other road users giving way.
 
NMC and HCPC registered healthcare professionals also work on call and we think this could improve the efficiency of attending to these duties.
 
We think CFRs dispatched to emergencies on behalf of state ambulance services would benefit from improved response times without the risks of blue lights.

Reduce VAT for the hospitality sector to no more than 10%, We would like a VAT reduction for the hospitality sector in order to support hospitality businesses, many of which are struggling through no fault of their own., Implement a significant reduction in Value Added Tax (VAT) rates applicable to the hospitality sector. We believe this reduction is vital to alleviate the financial burden on businesses and stimulate consumer spending, ultimately aiding in the hospitality sector’s recover.
 
The UK Government can play a pivotal role in safeguarding the future of the hospitality sector, preserving jobs, and revitalizing local economies.

Stop gchq employees and contractors parking on the residential roads in the area, Daily from 5.30am we get gchq employees parking on our roads, they slam doors, don’t use the gchq parking provided, the residents are now having to park on grass verges and I have even had gchq staff claim to be police and threaten me, I reported this to gchq police and they did nothing., We would like government to make gchq supply parking for their staff and contractors so they cannot park overtaking our local roads and affecting the values of our properties. GCHQ have plenty of parking and should be working for the people not against them

Make all dating sites require official identity documents for verification, I would like the Government to make dating sites require proof of ID through official documents when signing up, to stop discreet and fake profiles being made., I believe tackling the rise of fake profiles through requiring identity verification could reduce the number of people at risk of negative experiences and assault.
Stop west Berkshire council take away the dog bins in linear park (East), Get West Berkshire to reverse there decision on what they propose for they 2024/25 financial year,

Make Food Manufacturers provide both Oven and Air Fryer Instructions, I'd like the Government to introduce a bill amending any relevant bills, so that it is a legal requirement for Food Manufacturers selling packaged food (e.g: Branded and Own Brand products) in the UK (regardless of Point of Origin), to provide Air Fryer Instructions alongside Oven Instructions., Air Fryers are becoming commonplace in the household, most notably as a result of the Cost of Living Crisis making people search for more affordable ways to cook food. Air Fryer instructions do not always exist alongside Oven Instructions; Changing this, would help make Air Fryers more useable everyday, and in effect, reduce household costs.

Ensure the Crystal Palace RC track is retained as part of the park regeneration, As part of the regeneration the track has not been included in the plans.
Can you help the members of this 40 year old club ensure the developers add the track into the plans for the park to be used by the local community as has been for many years., We need to ensure a small area of the park is retained for the track.
The area is approximately 60m x 40m is a simple tarmac area that is enclosed by fencing.

Make Level 2 Understanding Autism mandatory across all education and businesses, Make it mandatory for all schools, higher education, businesses and public services to have at least 1 person trained in Level 2 Understanding Autism at a minimum. There needs to be someone in the building/on shift/available at all times for students, employees, employers, customers and the public., In 2022 I left university and my studies because I felt they did not understand autism or my needs. I felt the whole 18 months I attended were a constant battle of me repeating my needs. I believe this could have been avoided if they had better understood the adjustments I required.

Introduce new air quality and PPE rules for health and social care settings, We want the Government to set new rules on air quality and infection control in health and social care settings, to prevent and control airborne infections, with new ventilation and filtration requirements, new PPE standards and staffing rules, and monitoring and inspection to ensure compliance., Covid and other infectious diseases are spread by airborne aerosols. There are key ways to prevent them, by improving air quality and using well-fitting respiratory masks. Some research has found that reinfection can increase the risk of long-term serious organ damage and care workers having amongst the highest prevalence of long Covid. There are many tools to protect people in health and social care, including improving ventilation/air filtration, reintroducing PPE masks and Covid testing, and supporting ill staff to stay home.

Do not require XL Bully dogs to be muzzled until 18 months, I would like the Government to change the rules around the recent XL Bully dog ban that came into force on the 31st December 2023, stating that all XL Bully type dogs should be muzzled and walked on lead., I believe that Bully XL dogs under the age of 18 months should not have to wear a muzzle in public but should still be walked on a lead. I feel it is unfair to muzzle any dog before the adult age of 2. I believe early months are crucial to development and that dogs under this age rarely shows aggression to attack. Being able to socialise plays a huge role in a dog's life.

Review the implications of Ethiopia-Somaliland MOU for East Africa, We urge the Government to assess the potential impact of the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between Ethiopia and Somaliland, and consider whether any action is needed to safeguard regional stability and diplomatic norms., We are concerned that the MOU risks significant repercussions, including: 

1. Regional instability

2. Terrorist group attraction

3. Disruption to the Sea trade route

4. Formation of unnecessary alliances

5. The region becoming a battleground

6. Potential fragmentation of stable African borders

7. Potential unilateral recognition by Somalia of Somali regions in Ethiopia and Kenya

We want the Government to assess these risks, and intervene diplomatically if necessary.

Cap all parking fines in train station carparks to the cost of a day’s parking , I believe motorists are suffering because of the behaviour of some private car parking organisations that operate train station car parks. , I believe there should be a new law that caps all car parking fines in train station car parks to the amount a parking permit would cost for a day.

Increase funding to improve access to NHS dental services in England, We believe NHS dental services are at an all-time low. The NHS system is failing to meet the needs of many people who cannot afford private treatment. We want the Government to increase funding for NHS dental services so everyone can register with an NHS dentist and access NHS dental services., We believe the country is at a crisis point regarding dental services. Many people simply can't register with any dental practice. There are accounts of people performing unsafe DIY dentistry, for example extracting their own teeth and using super glue to try to fix crowns and dentures. You might expect this in third world Countries but we are in 21st Century England. Let's make our country Great again by improving dental service for everyone.

Extend seafarers tax exemption rules to offshore drilling sector, Allow UK seafarers working in the Oil & Gas industry, on UK registered ships the ability to apply for seafarers income tax reductions, irrespective of what their ship is designed to do, or is engaged in. Other trades that carry our their work on a ship can claim tax back., We think that rules around whether sea workers can claim this deduction should not be based on the type of ship they work on, and should be expanded to offshore installations. This would allow more sea workers to claim these deductions. Sea workers might carry out the same duties, but some be unable to claim this deduction, purely because of the type of ship they work on.

Award Mr Alan Bates a CBE for his service to the Post Office and Justice, Ask the prime minister to urge the king to award an appropriate honour now., Mr Alan Bates lead the campaign for justice for postmasters and postmistress a campaign fought over many years that is now seen as one of the biggest scandals of our time. His efforts along with many others should be acknowledged at the highest level this country can offer.

Remove VAT from student pilot training, The current cost for pilot training in the UK has risen over the past years making it very difficult for most to achieve it. The cost of training for a commercial license in the UK has now risen up to as much as £130000 which, in most cases is far too expensive for many people including myself., Most vocational training is exempt from VAT but pilot training is not. Nearly all students are self-funded and many find it very difficult to keep up with the rising costs of flying hours and studying. By removing the VAT it would make the cost of training for students much lower. The cost of training for a commercial licence usually range anywhere between £50000 - £130000, making it unachievable for most due to lack of grants, scholarships and financial assistance like bursaries. We believe action must be taken to avoid a shortfall of pilots.

Ban schools from letting trans students stay in dorms of their preferred gender, According to recent news report, boarding schools are allowing trans pupils to stay in dorms of their preferred gender. We think this is inappropriate, and schools should be banned from allowing this.,

Stop sale of Arundel Road council car park, Arundel Road council car park:
To my neighbours on the trading estate,

The council carpark behind MAK electricals on Arundel road is being sold for development.

Postcode: UB8 2RP

Freehold land registry title no. AGL199136

This would cause huge parking issues for the estate., The problems this will cause are:

    Parking chaos for estate
    More traffic from development
    This area is a zone 2 flood risk. Clearing the land will increase risk of flood to businesses
    Green belt land is eligible to be cleared and have temporary structures on it (cargo containers) - increasing flood risk further
    Otters inhabit the Colne river. Destruction of habitat may change this
    The UK has 98% of the chalk rivers in the world. The Colne river is one of them.

Require every police force to use the Interim Exemption Scheme, This scheme applies to dogs suspected of being a prohibited type under section 1 of the Dangerous Dog Act 1991. If the dog is not considered to be a risk to public safety, this would allow a dog that has been seized to be released and returned to their owner pending a court hearing., This would reduce the number of dogs and the length of stay in a kennel environment.

Allow XL Bully dogs to be off lead in public whilst wearing a muzzle, Due to the XL Bully ban many dogs are now not able to exercise in public off lead. Given that they are required to wear a muzzle to prevent injury to others and also have third party liability insurance, we want the Government to amend these rules to allow XL Bully dogs to run and play off the lead., Many people cannot afford, or do not have access to private land. Many private fields for hire do not allow XL Bully dogs at all, or require them to be on lead and muzzled if with another dog for insurance purposes. This means many dogs may experience physical health issues due to infrequent or inconsistent amounts of exercise. They will also not be able to socialise as easily with other dogs, which could impact their wellbeing and temperament. We believe this is not conducive to their welfare and will cause long term problems.

Hold a referendum on replacing the monarchy with an elected head of state
, We would like to see the Monarchy abolished and the Monarch replaced with a democratically elected Head of State., The British people have never had a vote to remove the Monarchy. This option has never in British history been asked. Let us decide for ourselves if we want a Monarchy.

"All humane things are subject to decay; And, when Fate summons, Monarchs must obey."

Fund more weekend/school holiday facilities for neurodiverse children, We would like the government to fund specialised facilities for children with neurodiverse conditions to be able to enjoy sensory play together on weekends and school holidays. We believe there is currently very little for children with Autism Spectrum Disorders or ADHD to enjoy safely anywhere., There should be accessible places for neurodiverse children to go to every weekend and school holiday to play freely no matter what the weather. We think there are nowhere near enough indoor spaces specifically for neurodiverse children to enjoy that are accessible.

Neurodiverse children deserve to have a place to go each weekend and in school holidays that is tranquil, sensory and helps their social skills and mental wellbeing.

Fund music at state schools to the amount spent by private schools, We believe that the enrichment an experience of music-making offers is disproportionately valuable in terms of stimulating the imagination and creativity of students in other areas. Studies have found that schools with good quality music often have higher academic outcomes in other fields., Many private schools advertise the value of music for the 7% of children who attend them. We believe the other 93% deserve the same benefits. We believe the Government pays lip service to the value of music (£6.7bn to the UK economy in 2023, with exports of £4bn) but fails to back words with actions. We believe the music teaching skills needed for the next generation are in danger of being lost, and that this would be a catastrophe for Britain's standing in the world, as well as for the welfare and wellbeing of its citizens.

Ensure that benefit assessors are trained in autism
 
, I think that benefit assessors often don't fully appreciate how autism can impact people and this can lead to people being refused benefits unfairly. I want all benefit assessors to be trained in autism, to try and ensure claimants are treated fairly, and not denied benefits unjustly., Being autistic can severely impact someone's ability to go about their daily life. I think that if benefit assessors received training in autism, they would be more understanding of this when conducting assessments. This could help ensure people with autism are treated fairly during the assessment process.

Make school uniforms VAT exempt, We want the government to pass legislation to make school uniform VAT exempt., By removing VAT on school uniforms it will help to reduce the financial burden on struggling families. It will help all students have the same attire regardless of their financial situations. We also believe that this will benefit schools as it will allow them to follow the British values of equality. School uniforms are a requirement and it may set families back further in their financial troubles. But by removing VAT it could help families with difficult financial situations to be treated equally.

Fund free parking for NHS staff whilst on shift, We want the Government to fund free parking for NHS staff whilst on shift across the UK., I and many other staff currently pay to park to go to work to look after people and save lives. For me this costs £20 per month (£240 a year). At some NHS facilities the amount per month goes up the more you earn.
 
I want the Government to find free parking across the board for all NHS staff working no matter what shift pattern you are on.

Make Care Experience a Protected Characteristic across England, Make 'care experience' a protected characteristic. This could give care leavers a higher chance of positive outcomes in their future and stop discrimination against people with care experience., If the government were to make care experience a protected characteristic it could help reduce discrimination and send a message that the rights of care experience people should be protected. Care leavers face poorer outcomes in their physical and mental health, education, employment and housing. This might be improved by making it a protected characteristic.

Add asexuality to the relationships education curriculum, Ensure the discussion of and teaching about asexuality, demisexuality, aromanticism, aro-ace and other forms of asexuality are included in the national curriculum for relationships education. It should become a mandatory part of teaching in schools, along with discussion of other LGBTQ+ topics., Asexuality plays a large part in many people's lives. They are incredibly important to many, and yet there is often little if anything taught about asexuality. This can lead to feelings where children, at the most vulnerable stage of life, are growing up feeling things are wrong with them, that they are different, and they may stay unaware for a long time of their life, possibly leading to horrific outcomes.

Reduce VAT rate for restaurants to 15%, We want the government to reduce the VAT rate for restaurants to 15%.

I am a Sheffield restaurant owner and our city like many others is seeing restaurant after restaurant close down., Livelihoods are being lost daily due to the ongoing rise in cost of food, fuel, utilities, staff wages, and the cost of VAT on top of this. We think that VAT is set at a rate that is too high and restaurants cannot claim enough back.
Review the decision to class double cab pickup trucks as cars for BIK purposes, This will mean an additional £5000 tax burden for those who use double cab pickup trucks for personal use.,

Fund increased pay for Teaching Assistants, We think the Government should fund increased pay for Teaching Assistants. People are struggling enough as it is and some Teaching Assistants need to take on a second job. We think more people need to know how low our pay is., As a hard working Teaching Assistant myself, I know how much I do in a day and feel that I deserve to be paid a lot more. People are leaving their roles as Teaching Assistants (due to the low pay) and I think that soon schools will be understaffed. I think there are jobs advertised and nobody is applying for them, because people qualified as TAs know how low the pay is. I believe something needs to be done before schools are in crisis.

Remove the booking system for Cheltenham Recycling Centre, The local authority (Cheltenham Borough) have been trying to dwindle the site down for years. We need the facility open as it has been without a booking system, Having a booking system will create more fly tipping as people who work full time will not be able to get appointments they require. The local streets will have more waste

Ban car meets in large car parks and introduce new requirements for landowners, We have seen unauthorised car meets taking place in large car parks both in out of town retail parks and in retail parks that are adjacent to community housing. We think they are unsafe, cause noise pollution could pose a risk to safety., We think we need legislation to hold landowners to account to ensure large car parks are only used for their intended purpose and introduce serious legal recourse to drivers. We think local communities are having difficulty holding attendees to account and car park landowners should be required to install and maintain barriers and ANPR cameras. These are costly and often landowners don't want to spend on this. We also think offenders should be fined and have points added to their licences.

Ban organisations from asking for a title (e.g. Miss, Mrs, Ms, Master and Mr), Ban asking for a title (Miss, Mrs, Ms, Master and Mr) when asking for a person's details. We think that disclosing a title is intrusive, unnecessary, out-of-date and sexist. We think that titles should be removed and we should adopt a gender-free, equal stance., We think that terms used for describing a woman are used in everyday situations that have nothing to do with ones marital status. We think that Mr, originally an abbreviated term for Master, is out-dated and sexist. Unless in a medical situation, we think one's sex is irrelevant. We do not think that knowledge of a person's marital status is required either. If someone needs to know the sex of a person, it could be a simple, M or F, but only if absolutely required.

Increasing funding to support children with special educational needs, We want the Government to provide more funding for:
 
- facilities to support children and give respite to parents during holidays
- special needs resources
- school places for children with additional needs
- sensory assessments for young children
, I think there are too few groups children can attend with SEND. I think we need more local facilities to offer this. I think school places for those with SEND are too limited for those with additional needs, and knowing that children with SEND can be nurtured through schools which can cater for their needs. I want more local funding to support these children.

Exempt all delivery drivers from parking fines, We want the Government to make it so that parking tickets can't be issue to courier drivers with official company vans and/or company signage in windows.,

Fund Topical Steroid Withdrawal (TSW) Research and Provide Support for Sufferers, We think research on TSW is crucial in creating diagnostic criteria, also to inform prevalence and aid in prevention. There’s growing awareness about the potential side effects of topical steroids, but until there is more action to address this, we are concerned patients will continue to suffer. , We urge funding allocation for the following:
1. Research to establish: susceptibility, diagnostic criteria, variations in expression, patient experiences/history of steroid use, and suggested maximum dosage.
2. Mental health support is crucial due to often severe psychological challenges faced alongside physical symptoms.
3. Education for GPs and dermatologists on TSW to support patients currently suffering and aid in preventing future cases.

Reopen applications for XL Bully dog certificate of exemption, We would like the XL Bully certificate of exemption process to be reopened for applications from people who couldn't get their XL Bully dogs exempted within the first exemption period., Many people were unable to make their XL Bully dog exempt before the deadline, due to lack of funds or knowledge of the situation at the time. We would like it to be reopened because there are a huge number of XL Bully dogs that weren't exempted at the time of the first process and there are still thousands of people's family pets that we believe still need to be made exempt.

School Minibus Safety - Remove Section 19 Exemptions for Schools, We call on the Government to remove Section 19 exemptions for schools in the Transport Act 1985, so children and young people are only driven by qualified, professional drivers, and that minibuses are maintained to commercial standards, by requiring a full Public Service Vehicle Operator’s Licence., In November 1993, a minibus carrying young people home to a Worcestershire school from a school trip to London crashed into a lorry, killing 13 people. The trip took place after the school day and the crash occurred just after midnight. We lost our daughter Claire in that crash.
A teacher, or support staff member can still, thirty years later, work all day, and then drive a school minibus for long distances without further training or qualifications.
All children, young people and staff must Come Home Safe.

Abolish Prevent Strategy, We want the Prevent Strategy to be abolished., We believe the Prevent policy has become a political tool to mark anyone with ideas different to those of the main parties.
 
We are concerned that any Government can add or remove themes and ideologies that could bring them political benefits.
 
We think that under the new definition of extremism many people in UK, including supporters of established political parties, could be covered by the the Prevent Strategy.
 
We believe the definition and prevention of terrorism should be done by specialists.

Ban the sale, propagation and planting of the invasive plant: Spanish Bluebell, I want the Government to ban the sale, propagation and planting of the Spanish Bluebell., The Spanish Bluebell is an invasive and quick propagator that is outcompeting our native English Bluebell in many areas. It can be difficult to eradicate from a garden and quickly spread via air (seed) and underground (bulb) from one garden to the next. This can cause disputes. It is readily available for sale online and in garden centres with no warnings about it's capacity to spread and carpet entire areas.

Remove Sunday Trading Laws, Remove Sunday Trading Laws so that large shops can trade as freely on Sundays as any other day of the week., The Sunday Trading Act was introduced in 1994 but society has changed significantly since those days. More and more people work unconventional hours and having one day of the week reduced to just 6 trading hours makes planning your days off tricky. Additionally, this could be beneficial to the employees of these sites as they may have more hours available to them to earn more. This could also lead to more Income Tax paid to the government and increased VAT revenue from the additional sales.

Ban parking time restrictions at motorway services, Due to times needed for EV charging and the demands at the charging station within services, and people requiring downtime on long journeys we want parking time limits at services to be banned.
 
, I request immediate action to reform parking arrangements at motorway services. We believe the 2 or 3 hour parking time limit at many services is now massively outdated, with not enough infrastructure for a fast turnaround in the services with the lack of EV chargers and the quantity of people needing downtime.

Do not support the Health and Equality Acts (Amendment) Bill, I am concerned that the Bill would restrict access to gender affirming care for trans children, such as hormone therapy. It would mean that healthcare professionals who provide this care could be prosecuted., I think the Bill could prevent trans children from socially transitioning at school and could lead to an increase in serious mental health problems among transgender youth, with potentially tragic consequences.
 
I think the Government should listen to real stories and consider the future for transgender individuals, to help create a safe, more accepting world. I believe this Bill would challenge current efforts to help marginalised groups and could worsen mental health issues in the UK for those who are transgender or questioning their gender identity.

Introduce a mandatory buffer zone for all new quarry sites, We want the Government to introduce a national minimum requirement for all new quarry sites to be at least 1,500 metres away from all residential settlements (10 or more homes), schools, hospitals and care facilities., Silica dust can displaced onto areas that are adjacent to quarries. Silica dust can be very hazardous to health, impacting young children and the elderly in particular, and can lead to silicosis. Silicosis can lead to other serious lung diseases such as COPD and lung cancer. One study of US quarry sites found levels of silica in the air nearby were 10 times higher than recommended exposure limits.

Recognise nonbinary people's genders in law and in identity documents, The UK government has repeatedly acknowledged the existence of nonbinary people, but it has repeatedly refused to grant recognition in law and systems., Nonbinary genders should be recognised on:
- Passports
- GRCs
- Marriage documents
- Death certificates

Review and reform VAT for registered mental health service providers, We want the UK government to:
 
Extend VAT exemption to all registered mental health service providers, including counsellors and psychotherapists.

Conduct a comprehensive review of the impact of VAT on access to mental health services., We call for VAT exemption for all registered mental health service providers, including all counsellors and psychotherapists, akin to VAT exemptions for clinical psychologists, to improve mental health access. Evidence shows these services can help reduce healthcare costs by offering effective treatment for anxiety and depression, aiding early intervention. This policy could lessen the £100 billion annual economic impact of mental health issues in the UK, promoting a more inclusive and equitable healthcare model.

Fund criminal justice, improve criminal bar fee structure, add organisation., Improved fee structure will provide certainty, junior barristers struggle to cover costs. Incentives for future barristers joining the criminal bar is low, perpetuating issues. Improve case file management systems. Give chambers guidelines to protect barristers from being overworked or abused., The law is about providing certainty and from submissions from barristers during my judge marshalling. Their is no certainly in practice due to a lack of criminal barristers. Workloads are being unfairly placed on barristers by clarks, mainly due to the amount of work not reflecting the amount of barristers. Legal aid only touches amendment, complications surrounding fee structures, increase avoidance of this area of practice. Organisationally changes have been made that are counterproductive.

Make the auditing of commercial premises on social media platforms illegal, We think the Government should amend the law to stop what we see as the harassment of commercial businesses by "social media auditors", who have no legal jurisdiction and may not have relevant qualifications., We think some businesses are being harassed daily by content creators who film staff reactions and post the footage on social media platforms. Sometimes this is for monetary gain and without consent. Also, we think that sometimes the legal use of drones is abused to record footage of private land which can be seen as an invasion of privacy as well as a security threat.

Require accessible adult changing facilities at all public toilets, Make it law that there should be changing facilities equipped with a large changing bed and hoist wherever there are general public toilets, open 7 days a week, 24 hours a day. These should require a RADAR key to avoid vandalism., We believe provision of changing facilities are inadequate, and that this seriously limits the lives of those that need to use them. It can mean young people and adults are unable to access the community equally due to a chance of being unable to be changed whilst not at home.
 
Would you like to sit in soiled underwear for up to an hour until the nearest changing places? No. Neither do disabled young people and adults.

Exempt people with severe mental health conditions from prescription charges, I would like those with severe mental health conditions to be made eligible for free prescriptions. , Managing severe mental health conditions can require daily medication to control symptoms triggered by stress. The financial burden of multiple medications can add stress. Skipping meds due to cost could lead to costly hospitalizations that outweigh the cost of free prescriptions. Staying medicated can be vital to stability, preventing further healthcare costs. If people stop taking their meds, it can be very dangerous to themselves and to others so it is vital that they can continue to do so.

Protect the national flags of the four union countries and the UK union flag, We want the Government to stop commercial businesses and any other persons or organisations from changing the way our national flags appear. We believe this is a violation., We think it will take an Act of Parliament to protect our national flags.

Reclassify general aviation airfields as greenfield not brownfield sites, Airfields around the country are categorised as brownfield sites making them attractive for development of housing estates. , However, airfields are often mostly grass land. Reclassifying them as green belt could help protect our green countryside, protect local employment and protect general aviation.

General Aviation airfields are home to wild flowers, plants and grasses as well as many small animals and birds such as Skylarks which are on the red list. Many future commercial pilots start their training at these airfields
 
We can protect GA airfields from being so vulnerable to closure by designating them as greenfield sites. This could help to achieve the government’s strategy to achieve JetZero and NetZero- as well as help to cement the UK as a world leader in general aviation.

Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal, We believe neither the Government, nor anyone else, should be able to use technologies to intervene in the Earth’s natural systems. We want all forms of 'geo-engineering' on land, sea and air in the control to be banned., The Government has said 'geo-engineering' is essential to meet its climate targets: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/geo-engineering-research-the-government-s-view/uk-governments-view-on-greenhouse-gas-removal-technologies-and-solar-radiation-management#why-they-are-needed
 
We want 'geo-engineering' to be banned.

Immediately Reintroduce Private Parking Code of Practice, I am campaigning on behalf of 35 million motorists for the Government Private Parking Code of Practice to be immediately reintroduced. We believe inadequate regulation of private parking frustrates the lives of millions of motorists., I am an 85-year-old pensioner and have been pursued by a parking company for an alleged parking violation. The claim was eventually dismissed by the Royal Courts of Justice, but I want the Government to take action to protect motorists from unfair charges and claims.
 
The British Parking Association and the International Parking Community have announced that it will implement a new Code of Practice for private car parks, but it has been reported that this will not address important issues such as a cap on parking charges, debt recovery, or an independent appeals process.
 
We believe the private parking industry is trending toward anarchy and must be brought to order by re-launching the Government Code immediately.

Ban zero hour/term-time only contracts for teaching assistants, I think zero hour and term-time only contracts should be prohibited for teaching assistants. Fair employment legislation is needed to protect the rights for classroom assistants across the education system. All contracts should include paid annual leave., With the rise in children with special educational needs, we believe classroom assistants are an essential part of education, offering specialised educational support on a one to one basis or a small group. Some teaching assistant contracts are being offered on a part-time only basis, with only term time hours paid around minimum wage. This can mean low wages across the year and can contribute to a poorer standard of living.

Extend the Post Office (Horizon System) Offences Bill, This petition calls on the Government to amend the new legislation to exonerate         postmasters by extending its scope to encompass prosecutions by the Department of Work  and Pensions (DWP), and convictions that have already been considered by the Court of   Appeal., Our core belief is that the conviction of any postmaster for offences such theft or fraud, during the period of Horizon’s operation, should be deemed unsafe and therefore included in the mass exoneration, in order to rectify all past injustices.
 
Without this, even more Postmasters that endured the burden of a criminal record may die without their names cleared and their innocence acknowledged.

Add a recommended renewal date to UK Passports, Introduce a ‘Renew By’ date to be printed inside a UK passport which would clearly indicate the latest date by which a passport should be renewed in order to meet passport validity rules for other countries., In light of confusion regarding passport validity, which has resulted in families and individuals being turned away at the airport, we propose that a recommended renewal date be printed within the passport. This could help make people more aware of when they should be renewing their passport and not just the expiry date. This change could enhance the understanding of passport validity requirements, reducing the risk of travel plans being affected by outdated or soon-to-expire passports.

Stop fines and criminal charges for taking children on holiday in term time, The fines system and threats of criminal proceedings should be abolished. We believe the working class are being penalised for enriching their children's lives. We don't think fines affect the middle/upper class as much. , We believe working class families are being discriminated against and treated like criminals for creating essential bonds and memories by taking their children on holiday. It may be that school holiday trips are too costly, or it might be that set holidays prevent families from taking trips within the school holidays. We believe this is discrimination, no other way to put it.

Make it a specific crime for members of the public to pose as a child online, So called self-named "paedophile hunters" are pretending to be children online. We believe it should be against the law to do this just as it is illegal to target and exploit children online., The so-called hunters go online pretending to be children with the aim to entrap and convince those they speak to. It should be against the law for those who are not law enforcement to act as a child or pretend to be one.
 
This is the job for law enforcement. The hunters can turn up in groups, we believe often looking to start trouble. Make it an offence to be pretend to be a child or pose as a child online including SMS, text, social media, email etc.

Fund improved care and support for individuals with FASD, Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is a disability affecting both children and adults, but there is a lack of awareness among healthcare professionals and the public. Consequently, individuals with FASD can struggle to access appropriate care and support services., We urge the Government to increase funding that goes towards improving care and support for individuals with FASD by:
 
1. Increasing funding for research into effective interventions and treatments
2. Funding the development of comprehensive training programs for healthcare professionals on how best to diagnose and treat individuals with FASD
3. Providing increased resources for families caring for loved ones with FASD
4. Funding public awareness activities about the risks associated with alcohol consumption during pregnancy
 
We believe it is time that the Government takes action on this critical issue affecting so many lives across our country. We urge it to act swiftly in implementing these changes so that individuals affected by FASD can receive the care they need.
